build: Commodore 64 Club issue 14, disk side B (a freezer backup of the title screen)

exclude: the bitmap of play and, on the title, the copy of the font at $CE00 that $CDC0 makes at $2800: output, cleared by the title routine at $16B3
KERNAL ROM, banked in throughout ($01 = $36); the RAM beneath is all zero in the image

comments.text: 6510 data-direction register for the port at $01. The game never writes it; the freezer's restore leaves it at $2F (orientation.md).

6510 port: memory banking. The game writes $36 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF, I/O at $D000, KERNAL ROM at $E000) at $0878 in the start-up and again at $9267 (bitmap-mode switch) and $92F9, and never changes it afterwards; the Supermon monitor's entry also writes $36, at $96F5.

Room 6's object flag: cleared at $61EA (the new-game reset of rooms 6 and 8), set to $20 at $645A when Mr Hat takes room 6's object (with $D8 = $50, $F5 = $28 and the status cells $07BE/$07E6 lit), tested for $20 at $6425 so the object can be taken only once. $0003-$0011 after it: BASIC workspace the game's traced code does not touch.

Room 6's interrupt counter: room 6's handler increments it every IRQ ($6099) and, while the room is lit, compares it with $40, $80 and $B0 ($615A-$6188) to time extra writes to $D022. Cleared at $681A (room 8's set-up) and $9594 ($9590, called from room 6's set-up end $5FBD). $0013-$001B after it: BASIC workspace, untouched.
Used only by the Supermon monitor ($9C09-$9ECC: stx/cpx/ldx); not by the game.
Used only by the Supermon monitor ($988D-$9ECA), a count loaded with $08, $16 or $03 and stepped down; not by the game.
Used only by the Supermon monitor ($9B36-$9E82); not by the game.
Used only by the Supermon monitor ($9C8D-$9E86, an index); not by the game.

Drawing-routine parameter: the number of rows to fill or copy. Read as the outer loop limit by the block copy $A400, the pattern copy $A42E and the fill $A451 (cpx $20), set by every caller (values 1-5 for pictures, $16/$17 for whole-screen fills at $A477/$A48B). The Supermon monitor also writes it ($9C3C).
Used only by the Supermon monitor ($9C40, $9D9E); not by the game.

Room 2's candle flag: set to $40 at $5519 when Mr Hat takes the candle in room 2 (after the sound call $1CE2), cleared at $61E1 by the new-game reset. Tested for $40 at $5ED8 and $5FC0 (room 6 drawn lit) and $7440 (room 9 lit), and for $00 at $8F1E (room 6's objects can be taken only with it) and $BDE2 (room 6's objects are drawn only with it).

Drawing-routine parameter: the width of a row. In bytes for the fill $A451 and the block copies $A400/$A42E (cpy $23; $A400 also adds it to the source pointer each row). In cells for the rectangle routines: $A67F fills that many screen-RAM cells per row (through $A620 and $A451), and $A690 multiplies it by 8 in place ($A6DE-$A6FC) before its bitmap copy $A400. Set by every caller before $A67F/$A690/$A451 (e.g. $17F0, $1803). The Supermon monitor does not use it.

Low byte of the drawing routines' destination pointer ($24/$25): screen RAM ($0400), colour RAM ($D800) or the bitmap ($2000), computed from a column and row by $A620 and $A690 and stepped by 40 (screen) or 320 (bitmap, adc #$40 plus inc $25) per row; written through with sta ($24),y at $A406, $A434, $A457.
High byte of the drawing routines' destination pointer $24/$25 (above): $04 screen, $D8 colour RAM, $20 bitmap as starting pages; incremented by the row stepping in $A41D-$A6D9.
Used only by the Supermon monitor ($983B-$9E92, an index); not by the game.

Drawing-routine parameter, two meanings: the fill byte for $A451 and for the rectangle routine $A67F (a screen-RAM colour pair such as $FF, $8C, $2C, $CC), or the low byte of the source pointer $27/$28 read with lda ($27),y by the block copies $A400/$A42E. Written by nearly every scenery routine (e.g. $17EC, $17FF). The Supermon monitor also uses $27,x.

Drawing-routine parameter: the high byte of the block copies' source pointer $27/$28 (e.g. $AC or $AD for pictures kept at $AC00-$ADFF, $3F for the picture at $3F60/$3F80), or the colour-RAM fill byte of the whole-screen colour fill $A48B (copied to $27 there). Callers also set it before the rectangle routine $A67F, whose colour-RAM half would have read it, but that half is switched off by the RTS at $A663. Also used by the Supermon monitor ($9B28-$9E5D).
Used only by the Supermon monitor ($9B2A-$9E6A); not by the game.
Used only by the Supermon monitor ($9A8A-$9E3F); not by the game. $002B-$0038 after it: BASIC pointers, not touched by the game.

Room 1 flag: cleared by the room's set-up at $1B9B, set to $40 at $1F17 when Mr Hat takes the item on the middle floor (the routine $1EDA, which also lights status cells $07BE/$07E6), tested at $4133. $003A-$003F after it: untouched BASIC workspace.

The score's thousands digit (0-9). The add-1,000-points routine $41DA redraws that digit from the digit glyphs at $1600 (status-line cells $3D38/$3E78, column 15), increments this count, and at 10 resets it ($4231) and carries into the ten-thousands digit ($45). Cleared by room 1's set-up at $1BBA. $0041-$0044: untouched.

The score's ten-thousands digit (0-9), counted by the carry code at $4243; at 10 it is reset ($4277) and the hundred-thousands digit (column 13, $3D28/$3E68) advances. That last digit has no counter: its glyph pointer $425B/$4261 is just stepped by $10, so past 999,000 points it would read beyond the digit table. Cleared at $1BBC. $0046-$0084 after it: BASIC workspace the game does not touch.
KERNAL I/O status byte (ST). Only the Supermon monitor touches it ($999F, $9A04); the game does not. $0091-$0092 after it: KERNAL workspace, untouched.
KERNAL load/verify flag, written only by the Supermon monitor ($99A1). $0094-$0098: untouched.

Jump step counter, reused by every room's movement code: each phase of a jump (up, across, down) counts it from 0 to $15 (21 steps) and clears it (room 1: $43A9-$444A; another copy at $49C3-$4A64; and in the other rooms' copies). Also read at $41BA/$41C0 (the jump sound) and, as a column, by the unreached routine $9100 ($9110-$914F). On a stock machine $99 is the KERNAL's input device number, which the game never uses.

Low byte of the KERNAL jiffy clock ($A0-$A2), advanced by the KERNAL IRQ that the game chains to at $EA31; read only by the Supermon monitor ($9ABA). It is one of the two bytes that differ between restart-title.vsf and handover.vsf. $00A3-$00AD: KERNAL tape/serial workspace, untouched by the game.
KERNAL end-of-load pointer low byte, written only by the Supermon monitor ($9A26).
KERNAL end-of-load pointer high byte, written only by the Supermon monitor ($9A2A). $00B0-$00B6: untouched.

Cleared by the room-1 set-up at $1B97 and never read by the game's code (the KERNAL's file-name length on a stock machine). The Supermon monitor writes it ($999D) and increments it ($99C7) when it parses a file name.
KERNAL secondary address, written only by the Supermon monitor ($999A).
KERNAL device number, written only by the Supermon monitor ($9998, $99E7).

Room 9's upper-door flag: cleared at $707E by the new-game reset, set to $26 at $78D3 once the upper door has been opened, and tested at $78DE, where $26 skips the door check (which otherwise opens the door when $F5 = $28, room 6's object, is carried). The Supermon monitor also uses it as the file-name pointer ($99A5, $99C5), its KERNAL meaning on a stock machine.
KERNAL file-name pointer high byte, written only by the Supermon monitor ($99A9).

Room 1's exit flag: set to $60 at $410B when Mr Hat takes the object on room 1's top floor (handler $40C0), cleared at $1BDF (room-1 set-up) and at $6061, $67FF, $7567, $7CD7, $839A, $8635, $967F; tested for $60 by the room-1 bottom-floor check $1EC5, which at X = $50 then jumps to $44C0 (room 1's way out). $00BE-$00BF: untouched.
Supermon monitor workspace ($C0,x at $9A6B-$9B13); not used by the game.
Supermon monitor's address pointer low byte ($C1/$C2, lda ($C1),y and the like, $9833-$9E99); not used by the game.
Supermon monitor's address pointer high byte ($9837-$9E9B); not used by the game.
Supermon monitor's second pointer low byte ($C3/$C4, $991C-$9B83); not used by the game.
Supermon monitor's second pointer high byte ($9920-$9B78); not used by the game.
KERNAL: the matrix number of the key its scan last saw (64 for none). The game reads it at $7C70, where 4 (F1) toggles $1019, at $C35F, and in the unreferenced F1 wait at $8000.

Footstep sound counter: $1D04, called on each walking step and each ladder step ($4B50, $4B84), increments it and every 11th call ($0B) plays a click on voice 2 and resets it to 0 (the KERNAL's reverse-mode flag on a stock machine). $00C8-$00D7: untouched KERNAL screen-editor workspace.

Game state flag. $40 = no lives left: set by $1734 when the last life mark is gone; every room loop tests it ($4469, $4A94, $51F4, $5A60, $6220, $6A20, $6DF3, $76B0, $8424, $86B0, $9320) and jumps to the game over $4475 (room 10's loop first points the IRQ back at $8215), and $1FDA, after a respawn, jumps to its second entry $447D. $50 = an object carried: set when a room's object is taken ($4E3B, $5CC8, $6467, $6D7D) and tested by each of those four takes ($4E0F, $5CAC, $642C, $6D61), so only one object is carried at a time; $00 = cleared when it is used ($540F, $78CF, $7992, $82B2). $00D9-$00F4: the KERNAL screen line-link table, untouched by the game.

Which object Mr Hat carries (with $D8 = $50): set when it is taken to $20 (room 2, $4E18), $EE (room 5, $5CD9), $28 (room 6, $646B) or $AF (room 8, $70AA); read where it is used: $549C (room 2, for $20), $78A0 and $78E4 (room 9's upper door, for $28), $796F (room 9's lower floor, for $AF) and $82AA (room 11, for $EE). The unreferenced ending fragment at $7D68 increments it.

Death-in-progress flag: $30 while Mr Hat is being killed (set at $4C71 and by the unreachable routine $1D53), $00 otherwise (cleared by the respawn $4D50 at $4D63, and at $4AA5, $5955, $1F9C, and by the loop at $50DF that clears $F6-$FE). Room 1's loop tests it at $42EF and then calls $1FD7 (respawn, or the title if no lives are left); room 3's loop tests it at $4C9A. The byte has other uses too: room 5's interrupt handler increments it every frame ($597C) and recolours the cones' cells at $40, $80, $B0 and $F0 ($598D-$59F8); the unreached routine $451F counts it up to $18 ($4542).

Cleared by the start-up at $0887; when it reads $20 the room-1 code jumps to $44B9 ($44AD, $6FEA). Its only other user is room 6's interrupt handler, which counts it from $00 every frame ($609C) and puts it back to 0 when it reaches $20 ($60EE-$60F7), so nothing leaves it at $20 and the room-1 tests cannot match; what it stands for is open.

Two uses. In room 1 it counts play frames: room 1's IRQ increments it at $1C90, and $1FAC-$1FB8/$449E-$44AA/$6FDB fire the event $44E0 when $F9:$F8 reaches $20:$F0. On ladders (the shared climbing step $4B20, used by rooms 2-11: $4B27-$4B6A) it is the animation delay, counted to 5 before $F9 steps. Cleared at $0889, $44C6, $4894.

Two uses. Paired with $F8 as the room-1 timer (set to $20 at $44C2; the event at $44E0 fires at $20:$F0). On ladders it is Mr Hat's climbing frame, $32-$33, stepped by the shared climbing step $4B20 at $4B38/$4B6C and copied to $07FC; set to $32 at $489D and $33 at $50F2, and copied to $07FC by room 6's sprite set-up at $6040. Cleared at $088B; also written by the unreferenced $816E ($8173).
Cleared by the start-up at $088D and set to $20 by the timed event at $44F9 (and to 0 by the unreferenced $816E at $8175); no reader found in the traced code.

Several uses. In play: the walking animation delay, incremented each step and reset at 9, when the walk frame advances (room 1 at $4307/$435B; cleared by the set-up $1B85 and at $400F), and the lift's delay counter ($4036, $406E). In the room drawing routines: the fill byte of the screen-RAM rectangle fill $56ED (e.g. $CC at $6E17). In the title music ($C1FC): the low byte of the note pointer $FB/$FC (lda ($FB),y at $C214, $C255, $C299).

Several uses. In room 1 it is the door flag: cleared by the set-up at $1B87, set to $20 when Mr Hat takes the object at X = $78 on the bottom floor ($1E79), and tested at $1E8F, where $20 lets him open the door at X = $A0. In the room drawing routines it is the width of the rectangle fill $56ED (cpy $FC). In the title music ($C1FC) it is the high byte of the note pointer $FB/$FC ($C20F, $C250, $C294).

Four uses. In play: Mr Hat's current walking-right sprite frame, $2C-$2E, advanced when $FB reaches 9 and copied to $07FC (room 1 at $4309-$4322; set to $2C at $1B8B). In the drawing routines: the number of rows of the rectangle fill $56ED (cpx $FD), the row count of copy_pattern_rows $5713 (cpx $FD at $572F), and the background colour argument of the room prologue $56B0 (ldy $FD at $56B8; for example $6E at $6E05, $98 at $65E2).

Low byte of the pointer $FE/$FF used by the title's bitmap clear $16B1-$16BB (sta ($FE),y) and by the room drawing routines ($56ED and many others) for screen addresses. Cleared by the room-1 set-up at $1B93.

Two uses. High byte of the pointer $FE/$FF ($16B5: $20, stepped to $3F by the bitmap clear). In play: Mr Hat's current walking-left sprite frame, $2F-$31, advanced like $FD and copied to $07FC (room 1 at $435D-$4376; set to $2F at $1B8F).

BASIC input buffer ($0200-$0258), used only by the Supermon monitor ($9BDC-$9EC5: its command-line and hex-assembly workspace, $0210,x). The game does not use it; the snapshot holds leftovers of a file name there ($0206: 'O"' and spaces, 'PRG' at $0214).
Supermon monitor workspace inside the BASIC input buffer ($9DB3, $9DC8, rotated with $0210 when it packs a number); not used by the game.
Supermon monitor's saved registers, $0239-$023F (written on entry at $9801-$9822, printed and restored at $9969-$998F): $0239 is the program counter high byte. Not used by the game.
Supermon monitor: saved program counter low byte ($9818, $9882, $98EA, $9978). Not used by the game.
Supermon monitor: saved status register ($980D, $997C). Not used by the game.
Supermon monitor: saved accumulator ($9809, $9980). Not used by the game.
Supermon monitor: saved X register ($9805, $9983). Not used by the game.
Supermon monitor: saved Y register ($9801, $9986). Not used by the game.
Supermon monitor: saved stack pointer ($9822, $996F-$9AED). Not used by the game. $0240-$0258: rest of the input buffer, unused.

KERNAL IRQ vector, low byte (CINV, with $0315). The game points it at its own interrupt routines: $EA31 (KERNAL only) at $16A6, $177A and $B678 (from $7CE8, after the last room), room 1's $1C00 at $1BF3, the other rooms' routines at $48A2 ($48B0), $50FC ($510A), $595A ($596A), $606F ($608A), $6831 ($683D), $75D1 ($7600), $820B/$842D/$8462 ($8215), $8647 ($8660), $90F3 ($B9AD); for the title music, $CB14 saves it and installs $C2EB ($CB22), which installs $C0AF at $C30A, and $CB0A puts the saved vector back. In the snapshot it holds $C0AF.
KERNAL IRQ vector, high byte; written together with $0314 by each of the installers listed there (with SEI/CLI around the pair in most of them).
KERNAL BRK vector, low byte: set to $66 (with $0317 = $FE: the KERNAL's warm start $FE66) at $92EF, and by the Supermon monitor at $97F0.
KERNAL BRK vector, high byte: $FE, written at $92EA and by the monitor at $97F6 (see $0316). $0318-$0353: the other KERNAL vectors (NMI, OPEN, ..., LOAD, SAVE), not written by the game's traced code.
KERNAL LOAD vector (ILOAD). Only the Supermon monitor uses it, jumping through it at $99EF; the game never loads anything.
KERNAL SAVE vector (ISAVE). Only the Supermon monitor jumps through it ($99F2).

The four lives marks are colour cells of the status line: $07B9 and $07BA (row 23, columns 33-34) and $07E1 and $07E2 (row 24), set by room 1's start of play ($6E6E, $6E71). A mark shows while its cell holds $BC and is hidden by $CC, grey on grey. $1D86, at the end of every death ($A8E6) and from $1D79/$1D82, takes the upper ones ($07B9, then $07BA at $1DB5) and then calls $1700 for the lower ones; room 3's $4C73 tests the upper cells for $6C, which never matches, and so goes straight to $1700; $1734 sets $D8 = $40 when the last is gone.

Sprite pointers $07F8-$07FF (screen $0400 + $3F8): shape number x 64 in VIC bank 0, so $24-$3F are the shapes at $0900-$0FFF. $07FC is Mr Hat's (sprite 4), the most-written byte of the game: walking $2C-$2E and $2F-$31, climbing $32/$33, crouching $2A, dying $27; room 3 also gives him $22 (the bytes at $0880, inside the start-up code) as he steps onto its ladder ($48F2, $4AFF).

The game's own BASIC program, as the freezer found it: the line 10 SYS 2157 ($0801-$080C, tokens 9E '2157'), then the text ' SYSTEM EDITOR<<<E **' at $0810 and, from $0828 to $0866, the tokenised tail of an older BASIC loader (SYS(PEEK(43)+256*PEEK(44)+127) at $084F), then $AA fill at $0868-$086C. Nothing reads these bytes; SYS 2157 enters at $086D.
Game entry, reached by SYS 2157. Calls the title $0876 (which returns when fire is pressed), falls into the new-game start $0870. Called once; the rest of the game re-enters at $0870.

Start a new game: $9265 switches the screen to bitmap mode, then $087E resets the game variables and enters room 1. Jumped to at game over ($802A, at the end of $8020, which $4486 reaches after the title), after the win ($7CF3), from $5BA4 (room 5, a path whose reachability is open), and from $8012/$801A in the F1 wait $8000, which only the dead Lupenio ending reaches ($7E24).
Banks the memory ($01 = $36: RAM at $A000-$BFFF, I/O, KERNAL) and runs the title routine $16A3, which returns once fire has been pressed.

Resets the start-of-game variables and jumps to the play set-up $6E00: silences SID voice 3 ($D40F frequency high = 0), clears $F7-$FA, sets $44E0 to $20 (restores the JSR opcode of the one-shot routine $44E0, which rewrites itself to RTS when it runs) and clears the sprite animation counters $64F0/$64F1.

Called from room 1's jump loops ($43AB-$443F, $4466), from $6FFC, and from the unreachable $1D20 ($1D30): when the sprite-enable register $D015 is $30 or more it runs the room-1 floor handler $1D33; otherwise it returns. The compare is on the whole register value, not on bit 4: it passes when sprites 4 and 5 are both on, or sprite 6 or 7 is on, and fails with Mr Hat (sprite 4) on alone.
Turns off every sprite but 4 (Mr Hat) and 5 ($D015 AND #$30). Its only caller, $45D0, is inside the unreached routine $451F, so it never runs.
Two zero bytes after the routine at $08AD; nothing reads them.

Bitmap graphics, three 8-byte cells ($08B8-$08CF, a shape sloping down to the left), read as one 24-byte block by $4573-$457E, which copies it to the bitmap at $36A0 (character row 18, columns 4-6); that copy is inside the unreached routine $451F.

Bitmap graphics, six 8-byte cells ($08D0-$08FF: the left and right edges of a picture, in pairs) that the loop $4580-$45A9 copies to the bitmap at $37E0/$37F0, $3920/$3930 and $3A60/$3A70: character rows 19-21, columns 4 and 6 (16 bytes apart, so column 5 between them is not written). The loop is inside the unreached routine $451F.
Cell at $08D8 of the wedge picture ($08D0): the right half of its top row, copied to $37F0 by $4588.
Cell at $08E0 of the wedge picture ($08D0): left half of the middle row, copied to $3920 by $458E.
Cell at $08E8 of the wedge picture ($08D0): right half of the middle row, copied to $3930 by $4594.
Cell at $08F0 of the wedge picture ($08D0): left half of the bottom row, copied to $3A60 by $459A.
Cell at $08F8 of the wedge picture ($08D0): right half of the bottom row, copied to $3A70 by $45A0.

Sprite shape $24 (64 bytes at $0900, multicolour): a figure with a round head and a long arm or stick held forward, legs below. Room 1's set-up puts it on sprite 6 ($1BC8); also set on sprite 2 at $BAB2/$BB06, where room 2's walker alternates it with $29 while walking right ($BAF3-$BB02).

Sprite shape $25 (multicolour): a creature with a small head and a wide body on many short legs. Sprites 0 and 1 in room 1 ($1B19-$1B1E) and sprite 0 in room 6 ($10A7); the shared IRQ tail $7000, used by several rooms' handlers, alternates it with shape $35 for their animation ($7007-$7033). Also sprite 3 on the title ($B7B7).

Sprite shape $26 (multicolour): a small dagger-like shape pointing right. Sprite 3 in room 1 ($1B26), the IRQ swapping it with its mirror image $34 when the sprite turns ($1C9C, $1CA4); also sprite 3 in rooms 3 ($463B), 5 ($592D), 9 ($7596 and its IRQ) and 11 ($8630, $8686), and sprite 4 on the title ($B7BC).

Sprite shape $27: Mr Hat's death frame, a work buffer. $1DDD copies a fresh 64-byte image into it from $ACD8 and points sprite 4 at it; $A8F0-$A913 then ANDs each of its bytes with the raster line $D012, so the figure crumbles away. The snapshot holds a partly worn copy.
Bytes 16-31 of the death-frame buffer $09C0 (sprite rows 5-10), worn away by $A8FB-$A901.
Bytes 32-47 of the death-frame buffer $09C0 (sprite rows 10-15), worn away by $A904-$A90A.
Bytes 48-63 of the death-frame buffer $09C0 (sprite rows 16-20 and the unused 64th byte), worn away by $A90D-$A913.

Sprite shape $28 (multicolour): a cabin with a window above a patterned base, the lift cabin: sprite 5 in room 1 ($1B32), moved with Mr Hat by the lift $4000, and in room 11 ($824F, the lift between its floors).

Sprite shape $29 (multicolour): the walker of shape $24 drawn in another pose. Room 2's walker, sprite 2, alternates it with $24 while walking right ($BAF3-$BAFC, through set_sprite2_pointer $BB06, from room 2's IRQ at $5110 via $BA7D); no immediate store of $29 to $07F8-$07FF exists, which is why it looked unused.
Sprite shape $2A: Mr Hat crouching, hat pulled down over a short body. Shown while the stick is held down ($4344 and the other rooms' copies).
Sprite shape $2B (multicolour): a cup or trophy on a stem, a guardian's shape. Sprite 2 in room 1 ($1B23) and in room 3 ($4888, a falling guardian), and sprite 6 in room 9 ($75AD/$75B0).
Sprite shape $2C: Mr Hat facing right, first walking frame (hat over a brim, two legs). The standing right frame: set at $1B2B and on every respawn facing right. Frames $2C-$2E cycle in $FD.
Sprite shape $2D: Mr Hat facing right, second walking frame; also the take-off frame of a jump to the right ($4398).
Sprite shape $2E: Mr Hat facing right, third walking frame, body leaning; also the landing frame of a jump to the right ($43D5).
Sprite shape $2F: Mr Hat facing left, first walking frame; the standing left frame. Frames $2F-$31 cycle in $FF.
Sprite shape $30: Mr Hat facing left, second walking frame; also the take-off frame of a jump to the left ($43F5).
Sprite shape $31: Mr Hat facing left, third walking frame; also the landing frame of a jump to the left ($4432).

Sprite shape $32: Mr Hat seen from the front, legs apart: his climbing frame on ladders, alternating with $33 in the shared climbing step $4B20 ($4B27-$4B76, through $F9); also set directly when he arrives on a ladder ($50B6, $753A, $8602 and others).
Sprite shape $33: Mr Hat from the front, second climbing frame (see $32).
Sprite shape $34 (multicolour): the dagger shape of $26 pointing left, set on sprite 3 by room 1's IRQ at $1CA4 when it turns, and by room 9's ($7652) and room 11's ($869B) handlers.
Sprite shape $35 (multicolour): the many-legged creature of $25 in its second frame ($7016, $7031).

Sprite shape $36 (multicolour): a round body with a pointed tip, first of four such shapes $36-$39. They are room 9's upper-floor guardian, sprite 0, which walks towards Mr Hat: $36/$37 walking right, $38/$39 walking left (room 9's IRQ, $7BA3-$7BD5).
False symbol: the operand of the Supermon monitor's BIT $0DA9 at $9D56, the skip idiom that hides LDA #$0D. These bytes are part of sprite shape $36 ($0D80).
Sprite shape $37 (multicolour): second frame of room 9's guardian walking right (with $36; stored at $7BAF).
Sprite shape $38 (multicolour): first frame of room 9's guardian walking left ($7BC9; see $36).
Sprite shape $39 (multicolour): second frame of room 9's guardian walking left ($7BD5; see $36).
Sprite shape $3A (multicolour): a creature with a cup-shaped body and two legs. Sprites 0 and 3 at $B99C and $BA2F, alternating with $3F.

Sprite shape $3B (multicolour): an octopus, eyes in a round head, tentacles below. Sprite 7 in room 1 ($A733), alternating with $3C in the IRQ chain at $A74B-$A75C; also sprite 3, the guardian stepped by $B877 (alternating with $3C every 5 frames) in rooms 3 ($4821), 4 ($9079) and 5 and wherever $B877 runs, and sprite 1 on the title ($B7AD).
Sprite shape $3C (multicolour): the octopus of $3B with its tentacles the other way.

Second entry of the title: first toggles the screen-enable bit with $A500 ($D011 EOR #$10, which blanks the bitmap the room left on screen), then runs the title $16A3. Called at game over ($447D) and from $7CF0.

The title screen. Points the IRQ vector back at the KERNAL's $EA31, clears the bitmap $2000-$3EFF through $FE/$FF (it stops at page $3F, so $3F00-$3F3F, the last 64 bitmap bytes, keep their contents), turns all sprites off, sets border and background to grey ($0C), and calls $CDC0, which copies the title font to $2800 and sets up the title text and its music interrupt ($C0AF). If the screen is blanked ($D011 bit 4 clear) it calls $A500 to show it again, sets the sprite multicolours to $02/$0D, and waits for fire in $1770; it returns to its caller when fire is pressed.

Removes one life mark from the lower status row, or ends the game: if the screen-RAM colour byte $07E1 (row 24, column 33) is $BC (mark shown) it becomes $CC (hidden); else the same for $07E2 (column 34); if both are already hidden it sets $D8 = $40, no lives left. Each branch also writes $D01E (AND #$EF, a write to the read-only collision register that has no effect), and the first two reset Mr Hat's colour $D02B to $0B. Called from $1DD0 after the upper marks $07B9/$07BA are gone, and from $4C93.

Returns to $16EE. The freezer snapshot was taken inside this loop ($1773).

Long runs of NOPs ($1850-$1869, $18F5-$193F with a stray LDY #$34 at $191D, $1953-$19B1) do nothing.

Low byte of the operand of STA $2BF8 at $18B3 (self-modified). The loop $18AC-$18D4 reads 48 bytes from $1191,Y (bytes that are also code: $1191 is the routine draw_pic_mc_sprite1) but stores them all to this one unindexed address, so only the last byte of each group of 48 ($11C0, $11F0, $1220, $1250, $1280) survives. After each group the high byte $18B5 is incremented and this low byte raised by $10 (one more increment of $18B5 on a carry), $110 in all, so the five survivors land at $2BF8, $2D08, $2E18, $2F28 and $3038. The same loop at $9167 has STA $35D8,Y, which with the index advancing places each group of 48 one character row ($140 bytes) below the last; here the index is missing. $18D7 puts the operand back to $2BF8.
High byte of the self-modified store address of the loop at $18AC (see $18B4): incremented on each carry ($18D1) and once per group ($18BC), reset to $2B at $18DC.
The two bytes of a LDY #$34 left among the NOPs; $1940-$1947 rewrites them with the same values ($A0, $34), so the store has no effect.
Second byte ($34) of the leftover LDY #$34 at $191D, rewritten unchanged by $1947.

Low byte of the operand of STA $2768,Y at $19EE, the second bar loop ($19E7-$1A1B, cells from $13F9), stepped like $19BA and reset to $68 at $1A14.
High byte of the STA $2768,Y operand of the second bar loop, reset to $27 at $1A19.
Draws the 'Mr.Hat' logo of the status line ($3F80) at column 0, row $17 (23) with $A702.

Second part of room 1's set-up (jumped to from $1A1E). Draws more objects ($A7D9 at $1A,$13 and at $14,5, $A7F8 at $14,7, $A782 at 2,$0C), the logo ($1A21), the status line: life marks $1449, the words SCORE, ROOM and STAGE, the score 000000 and the digits 1 for room and stage (from the tables at $1449-$1618 into bitmap rows 23-24). Then it sets up the sprites: enable $B2 (sprites 1, 4, 5, 7), multicolour $B7 (sprite 6 added at $1BD8), X high bit for sprite 5, sprite 5 double size, pointers ($25 $25 $2B $26 $2C $28 for sprites 0-5, $24 for 6), colours and start positions (Mr Hat, sprite 4, at X $85, Y $CC). It initialises the play variables (walk counters $FB-$FF, flags $B7, $39, $40, $45, $BD; the score digit pointers $41DD-$4261, so the score starts at zero), sets sprite 3's direction to DEC ($1C12), calls $802D, installs the IRQ $1C00 and jumps through $A817 to room 1's main loop at $42EF.
The operand of LDA #$2C at $1B9D, which the next instruction stores back into itself unchanged: a no-op left by an edit.

Room 1's interrupt routine, installed in $0314/$0315 by $1BF3. It runs a chain of jumps, each part ending in a JMP to the next: $AAB2 (when sprite 1's X is $80 or $00, redraws the two arrow pictures at column $23, rows 3 and $14, through $AA9A/$AA83, with screen colour $DC or $4C), $A73F (sprite 7's octopus frames, $3B/$3C every 8 ticks of $64F0), $1C03 here (the guardians' motion), $7000 (sprites 0 and 1 frames), $8215 and $BF30 onward, and finally the KERNAL's $EA31.

Moves room 1's guardians once per interrupt: sprite 0 one pixel right, sprite 1 two pixels right, sprite 2 one pixel down ($D005), sprite 3 one pixel left or right ($D006, its X; the opcode at $1C12 is DEC or INC). A sprite that reaches X $20 is switched on with a new height chosen from the raster line ($A944: sprite 0 at Y $94 or $86, $A960: sprite 1 at $5C or $4E), so it comes in on one of two floors at random; sprite 0 is switched off at X $D6, sprite 1 at X $E0. Sprite 2 is switched on at Y $46 and off at $D3. Sprite 3 turns at X $FD or more (DEC, now moving left, shape $26) and at X below $20 (INC, moving right, shape $34); this routine never switches sprite 3 on. Also counts sprite 1's animation timer $64F1. Ends with $1C90: INC $F8, JMP $7000.
Self-modified opcode: $CE (DEC $D006) or $EE (INC $D006), the direction of room 1's sprite 3. Written by the set-up ($1BE8: DEC) and by the turns at $1C4B (DEC) and $1C8A (INC).
End of the guardians' step: counts the play frame in $F8 and jumps to $7000 (the next link of the interrupt chain).
Unreachable bytes after JMP $7000: four NOPs and a second JMP $7000. No jump to $1C95-$1C98 was found.
Sets sprite 3's shape to $26 when it turns to move left (X reached $FD, $1C4E), and returns to the checks at $1C51.
Sets sprite 3's shape to $34 when it turns to move right (X below $20, $1C8D), and goes on to $1C90.
Unused zero bytes $1CAC-$1CAF before the sound routines.
Silences SID voice 1: zeroes $D400-$D406 (frequency, pulse width, control, envelope) and sets the volume $D418 to 15. Called before most of the game's effects (23 callers, $1E7E-$87BD).

An empty routine (a lone RTS) that six places call after $1CB0 ($1E81, $1EF2, $4E36, $5CC3, $6455, $6D78), in the place where a sound effect would be started. The zero bytes $1CC3-$1CD1 after it are unused.
Another empty routine (RTS) called where a sound would start, from $1EB3, $4168, $540A, $78C4, $79A2 and $82E1. The bytes after it, $1CD3-$1CE1, hold a sound routine that is never reached.
Unreachable: NOP, STA $D404 (voice 1 control from A), attack/decay $EE, frequency high 2, RTS: a sound effect left behind the RTS at $1CD2. No jump to $1CD3 was found.
A third empty sound routine (RTS), called from $40D8, $451A and $5514. $1CE3-$1CF1 after it: unused zeros.

Silences SID voice 2: zeroes $D407-$D40D and sets the volume $D418 to 15. 29 callers: the walking and climbing steps (room 1 and room 3's loops, the shared walk $5360/$5390, the ladder step $4B4D/$4B81, room 8's walk), which then play the footstep click $1D04; the main loops of rooms 2, 5, 6, 8 and 9; the jump routines of rooms 1, 11 and 4/7; and the lift check $1FA9.

The footstep sound: counts $C7, and on every 11th call plays a short noise on voice 2 (control $81, attack/decay 0, frequency high $FF) and resets the count. Called after $1CF2 by the walking code of each room.
Unreachable entry: sets voice 2 to a sawtooth note (control $21, attack/decay $11), loads $88, four NOPs, calls $08A1 and falls into $1D33. No call to $1D20 was found in a byte scan.

Room 1's per-step floor check (from $08A9): picks the handler for the floor Mr Hat stands on by his Y ($D009): below $5D the top floor ($40C0), below $95 the middle floor ($1EDA), otherwise the bottom floor ($1E20).
A spare RTS and a zero byte, then at $1D4C STA $D418 / RTS (set the volume from A), which nothing calls (byte scan for JSR/JMP $1D4C found none).

Kills Mr Hat: jumps to the death routine $A877 (the frame $27 that crumbles, the fall to the floor, the life lost and the respawn). Called by room 1's hazard checks ($1F32, $1F70-$1F97) and at $4128, $4505. While the player is invulnerable, $1250 has put an RTS at $A877, so this does nothing.

Unreachable: an older death routine behind the JMP at $1D50. It would set the death flag $F6 = $30, show frame $27 in white, copy the death shape ($1DDD), switch Mr Hat off and fall into $1D6D. No reference to $1D53 was found.

Puts Mr Hat back at the room's entry after a death, then takes a life ($1D86): X = $38 if he died on the bottom floor (Y $95 or more), X = $FE otherwise. Called from $A8EA, the death routine's branch for rooms whose screen cell $0400 holds $6E (in the others $A8E6 calls $1D86 directly and the position is left as it is).

Takes one life: hides the first life mark still shown, upper row first: if the screen-RAM byte $07B9 (row 23, column 33) is $BC it becomes $CC, else $07BA (column 34); when both are gone it hands over to $1700 for the lower row and the game-over flag. With each mark it also writes $CC to the background register $D021, reads $D01E (clearing the sprite collision latch), gives Mr Hat his colour $0B back and the standing frame for his floor ($1D9D).
Gives Mr Hat his normal colour ($0B in $D02B) and a standing frame: $2C (facing right) on the bottom floor, Y $95 or more, $2F (facing left) higher up.

Starts the death picture: saves Mr Hat's current frame in $1E05, copies the 64-byte shape at $ACD8 into the sprite block $27 ($09C0), and points sprite 4 at it. Called by the death routine at $A87D (and from the unreachable old death routine at $1D61).
A busy-wait of 48 x 256 loop passes, the pace of Mr Hat's sinking to the floor in the death routine ($A8B2, $A8CB).
Unused zero byte before the variables at $1E05.

Mr Hat's sprite frame at the moment of death, saved by $1DDD. The death routine reads it at $A880: if it was $32 or $33 (his climbing frames, set by the ladder step $4B20 and the room set-ups that place him on a ladder) he is not made to sink to the floor ($A8A0 is skipped).

Shared parameter, two uses: the left end of the X range tested by $A97C (X register in, compared with Mr Hat's $D008), and the saved column X of the picture routines $A9D2, $B800, $B83B, $BE60 and $BEAB, which draw a picture in several passes.
Shared parameter: the right end (exclusive) of $A97C's X range, or the saved row Y of the picture routines $A9D2, $B800, $B83B, $BE60 and $BEAB.

Written with $FA ($6084, $7074, $96A6), $CA ($711D) or A ($B982), and read by no instruction in the traced code (checked for indexed access too); its use is unknown. $1E09-$1E11 after it: unused zeros.

Twelve bytes, $0F $D2 $0C $8F $0B $DA $0A $8F $05 $47 $02 $A3, read by no instruction found (also not through an index). As big-endian words they would be SID frequencies falling in steps ($0FD2 ... $02A3), perhaps a tune or effect left unused. $1E1E-$1E1F: zeros.

Room 1, bottom floor (Y $CC), run on each step: first $A9B8 kills Mr Hat if his X is in $C4-$F3 while he stands on the floor, then by his X ($D008, 8-bit): at $20 he is pushed back right (the left wall); at $FF in the air he is moved back 6 pixels (the right wall); when the 8-bit X has wrapped to $00 on the floor, or is $01 at any height, $4000 runs (the lift) and sprite 5's colour $D02C (the lift cabin) is set to 3, while X $00 in the air moves him back 6 pixels; at $78, while the screen cell $072B is $B2, he takes the object there: cells $072B/$0703 are blanked ($CC), $FC = $20, $D022 is written ($2C, then INC), and $1CB0 (voice 1 off) and $1CC2 (an empty RTS) are called, so no sound plays; at $A0, while cell $06BC is $2C (the closed door), he opens it if $FC = $20 (cells $06BC/$06BD and $0734/$0735 become $1C; $1CB0 and the empty $1CD2 again) or is held back a pixel; at $50 with $BD = $60 it writes $D015 OR $C0 into the background colour $D022 (probably meant for $D015) and jumps to $44C0. Otherwise the guardian check $1F70.

Room 1, middle floor (Y $94), run on each step: at X $20 pushed back right; at X $30, while cell $060A is $B7, he takes the object there: $1CB0 (voice 1 off) and the empty $1CC2, background colour $D022 stepped three times, cells $05E2/$060A blanked, the status cells $07BE/$07E6 lit ($7C) and $39 = $40. With X in $80-$A7 and Y in $94-$A9 he is killed ($1D50, a hazard). At X $FF in the air he is moved back 6 pixels; X $00 on the floor, or $01 at any height, runs $4000 (the lift) and sets sprite 5's colour $D02C to 3; X $00 in the air moves him back 6 pixels. Then the guardian check $1F70.

The right-edge part of the middle-floor check $1EDA (reached from $1F1D, $1F22, $1F2B and $1F30 when Mr Hat is outside the hazard): wall at X $FF unless he is at floor height $94, lift ($4000) at X $00 on the floor or X $01 at any height, X $00 in the air moved back 6 pixels, then the guardian check.

Kills Mr Hat ($1D50) when the sprite-sprite collision register $D01E reads exactly $11, $12, $14, $18 or $58: sprite 4 together with sprite 0, 1, 2 or 3, or with sprites 3 and 6. Reading $D01E also clears it. Any other combination (two guardians at once, $13, or sprite 4 with 5 or 7) does not kill. Called by both floor checks and at $41A1.
Clears the death flag $F6 and switches every sprite off ($D015 AND #$00). Called from $451F.

Called first by the lift routine $4000: silences voice 2, fires the room-1 timed event $44E0 when the timer $F9:$F8 reads $20:$F0, and, once that event has run (its first byte rewritten to RTS) and Mr Hat is on the bottom floor (Y $CC), sets sprite 5's colour to 3, writes RTS over $1FBB so this part runs only once (put back to LDA by $706A), and jumps to $4469 in room 1's loop. The wait for $44E0 to become RTS ($1FBB-$1FD3) looks unreachable in play: $44E0 turns into RTS only through timer_oneshot_44e0, which needs $F9 = $20, and in room 1 $F9 gets $20 only at $44C2, on the path that leaves at once for room 3 (whose set-up clears $F8-$FF at $4894); room 1 has no ladder to step $F9 ($4B38, $4B6C). Traced, not tested.
The self-modified first byte of the once-only part of $1FA9: $AD (LDA $44E0) normally, $60 (RTS) after it has run ($1FD0); $706A restores $AD.
RTS that ends $1FA9 and is also the branch target of $1FDE.

Called by room 1's loop when $F6 = $30 (a death has happened): $4D50 puts Mr Hat back at the room's entry (X $38 facing right on the bottom floor, else X $FF facing left) and clears $F6; then, if $D8 = $40 (no lives left), it jumps to $447D: the title, then a new game.
A spare RTS after $1FD7, never reached.
An empty routine (RTS), called from $44DA in the timed event.
Leftover bytes $99 $8D $14 $03 $20 $B0 $1C $60 and zeros: the end of an older routine (STA $0314 ... JSR $1CB0, RTS) cut off at its start; not reached.

Unreachable copy of a floor-edge check like $1F4F: if Mr Hat's Y is $5C it calls the lift $4000 and sets $D02C = 3; otherwise its BNE goes to $1FDF, the operand byte of the BNE at $1FDE, where the bytes would run as INC $4C,X / ADC $6044,X / RTS. No call to $1FF0 was found.

Status line digits, two bitmap cells each (rows 23 and 24): the score's hundred-thousands $3D28/$3E68, ten-thousands $3D30/$3E70 and thousands $3D38/$3E78 (the three lower digits never change), ROOM $3D80/$3EC0, STAGE $3DB8/$3EF8, drawn from the glyphs at $1600.

The last 64 bytes of the play bitmap ($2000-$3F3F): character row 24, columns 32-39, the bottom-right corner of the status line. Output, not data: room 1's set-up writes the lower life marks into $3F08-$3F17 and clears $3F18-$3F27. The title's bitmap clear $16A3 stops at $3EFF, so these bytes survive a return to the title.
Bitmap cells of row 24, columns 33-34: the lower two life marks, copied from $1449 by $1A50-$1A5E (the upper two go to $3DC8). Whether each shows is decided by its screen-RAM byte $07E1/$07E2.
Bitmap cells of row 24, columns 35-36, cleared to zero by room 1's set-up ($1A6D-$1A78), next to the life marks; $3F28-$3F3F after them (columns 37-39) are not written by the traced code.

Scratch byte of the drawing routines at $A4AA-$A61C: the loop counter of the background fill $A4AA (0 to $14, twenty two-cell columns), the quotient of X / 16 in $A573, a saved $24 in $A50A, and a column offset in $A52F/$A5DC.
Screen-RAM fill byte of the room background (the colour pair of the bitmap pattern): $A573 stores Y here, and $A4EF hands it to the screen fill $A477 through $27. Also a saved $25 in $A50A.
Colour-RAM fill byte of the room background: $A573 stores X here and divides it by 16 (so X = $62 gives 6), and $A4F4 hands it to the colour-RAM fill $A48B through $28.
Low byte of the bitmap pointer of the background fill $A4AA, starting at $2000 and advanced by 16 bytes (two cells) per column.
High byte of the background fill's bitmap pointer (starts at $20, incremented on carry at $A4E5).
$A573 saves the caller's $27 (the pattern pointer, e.g. $60 of $3F60) here while it works, and restores it at $A5AA before the fill $A4AA.
Saved $28 of $A573 (e.g. $3F), restored at $A5AF.
Column of the rectangle routines: $A620 takes it from X and adds it to the screen address; $A690 restores it from $3F49 and steps the bitmap address by 8 per column.
Row of the rectangle routines: $A620 takes it from Y and counts it down while adding 40 per row to the screen address ($A634-$A645); $A690 restores it from $3F4A and adds 320 per row for the bitmap.

Copy of the rectangle's column kept by $A650, so that the bitmap pass $A690 can start again from it. The colour-RAM pass at $A665 that would also reread it ($A66D) is unreachable since $A663 became RTS.
Copy of the rectangle's row kept by $A631 (in $A620), reused by $A690 to address the bitmap. The reader at $A667 is in the dead colour-RAM half ($A665-$A67E, unreachable since $A663 became RTS).
Down-counter of $A690: first the columns while it moves the bitmap pointer across ($A6C2-$A6DB), then the width while it multiplies $23 by 8 ($A6E0-$A6F5). $3F4C-$3F5F after it: zeros, not used.

The room background pattern: 16 bytes, two bitmap cells of bricks. $56B0 points $27/$28 at it and calls $A573, and $A4AA repeats it over the whole play area (character rows 0-22, all 40 columns); the room's colours come from $3F41/$3F42. It lies past the end of the bitmap ($3F3F), where the VIC does not show it. $3F70-$3F7F after it: $FF then zeros, not referenced.

The 'Mr.Hat' logo at the left of the status line: a bitmap picture of 8 x 2 cells (128 bytes, $3F80-$3FBF the top row, $3FC0-$3FFF the bottom row). $A702 fills its screen bytes with $9C (it also passes $4C for colour RAM, but that pass, after the RTS at $A663, never runs) and copies it with $A690 to column X, row Y; room 1's set-up calls it through $1A21 with column 0, row $17 (23).
Bottom row of the 'Mr.Hat' logo (eight cells, drawn in character row 24 under $3F80's top row): the lower parts of the script letters and the underline.

Room 1: the lift ride. Called by room 1's floor handlers when Mr Hat's X low byte ($D008) is 0 or 1 on a floor (top $4195, middle $1F5D, bottom $1E4F): walking right past X=$FF on a floor wraps X to 0, and that is entering the lift. JSR $1FA9 first (silences SID voice 2, checks the $F8/$F9 timer and the $44E0 one-shot). Sets X=0, sprite pointer $07FC=$2F, delay counter $FB=0, sprite 5 (the lift cabin, X=$120 at the right in play-room1.vsf) colour 3. Then by Y ($D009): below $5D top floor, below $95 middle, below $CD bottom. Stick down (exactly $7D) on the top or middle floor, or stick up ($7E) on the middle or bottom floor, moves Mr Hat and sprite 5 together 56 pixels ($38 steps of $D009/$D00B, each with a 4x256 INC $FB delay) and returns. Stick left ($7B) sets sprite 5 colour 3 and returns, so the main loop's left step walks him out of the lift. Any other input loops back to $4000: the game waits here. Y $CD or more: returns. The BCS at $401B is always taken (CMP #$00 leaves carry set).

Operand low byte ($FC) of STA $07FC at $400A. Also read as data by LDA $400B at $102B in $1020 (called only from $A97C), masked with $F0: so $1020 always returns $F0, and $A97C's following CMP #$10 never matches.
always taken
Unreachable: JMP $4056 after the RTS at $4086; nothing jumps here (searched by bytes). A leftover of the lift code.

Called once at the start of each lift ride, before the 56-step move (down at $402B, up at $4063): INC $D021. In the play screen's hires bitmap mode ($D011=$3B, $D016=$C8 in play-room1.vsf) $D021 is not shown, so this has no visible effect.
Unreachable byte $25, the tail of an overwritten instruction (probably LDA #$25).
Unreachable leftover: sets SID voice 2 control $D40B (from A), attack/decay $D40C=$C0 and frequency high $D408=$04, RTS. Nothing calls it (searched by bytes).
Room 1 lift, no recognised input on the middle or bottom floor: back to the start of room1_lift_ride to wait.
Unused: a lone RTS ($60) and two zero bytes after the lift code.
Scratch byte (handover $01): written and read back by the routine at $1020 (STA/LDA $40BB, then AND #$0F into $1009).

Room 1: per-step handler for the top floor, called through $08A1/$1D33 when Mr Hat's Y < $5D. X=$20: pushes him right (left wall). X=$40 with colour cell $051B = $0C (the black 3x3 object at columns 3-5, rows 5-7 still there): takes it: JSR $1CB0 (voice 1 off), JSR $1CE2 (an RTS), six INC $D022 (no visible effect in hires bitmap), erases cells $04CB/$04F3/$051B (x3) with $CC, shows it in the status line (cells $07BC-$07BD, $07E3-$07E5 = $0C) and sets $BD=$60, which the bottom-floor handler checks at $1EC5 to open the way out ($44C0). X in $A0-$C7 with Y $5C-$7B (standing, not jumping): dies (JSR $1D50). X=$F8 with $39=$40 (set at $1F15 by the middle-floor pickup) and cell $0492 = $7C: recolours cells $0492-$0493, $04BA-$04BB, $050A-$050B to $1C (yellow object at column 26 turns white), voice 1 off; X=$F8 without it: one extra step right. The $F8 branch also does five INC $D022 and JSR $1CD2 (an RTS). X=$FF off the floor level ($5C): six steps left (the right wall stops jumps). X=0 at Y=$5C, or X=1 at any Y: the lift (room1_lift_ride). X=0 off the floor level: six steps left. Ends with JSR $1F70, the guardian collision test.
voice 1 off

A stray RTS ($60) inside room1_top_floor, between the JMP $412C at $4112 and $4116: nothing transfers to $4115 itself. The code after it is live: $4116-$41A4 (room1_top_floor_right) is the rest of room 1's top-floor handler, reached by the BCS $4116 at $4110 when X >= $A0.

room1_top_floor_right, the rest of room 1's top-floor handler, entered by the BCS at $4110 when X is $A0 or more (below $A0 the JMP at $4112 goes straight to the X tests at $412C). From $C8 on, and between $A0 and $C7 while Mr Hat is in the air (Y < $5C), on to the X tests; otherwise, between $A0 and $C7, the floor hazard: JSR $1D50 at $4128 for Y $5C-$7B (Y >= $7C, which the top floor never has, goes to $4139). The X tests at $412C, reached for every X but the hazard: X=$F8 the column-26 object when $39=$40 (else pushed right); X low byte $FF, or 0, with Y not $5C pushed six pixels left; X 0 at Y $5C, or X 1, rides the lift (JSR $4000 at $4195); then the guardian test JSR $1F70 at $41A1.
standing in the hazard: die
Room 1 top floor: the column-26 object, reached at X=$F8 when $39=$40 (and, by the BCS at $4126, for Y >= $7C, which the top floor never has).
Unused: 11 zero bytes after the room 1 top-floor handler.

Jump sound, called on each of the 21 rising steps of a jump (the first phase only; the level and falling phases are silent), two call sites per room: room 1 ($43A0, $43FD), room 3 ($49BA, $4A17) and the jump copies of the other rooms ($5241, $5AAD, $626D, $6A6D, $76FD, $86FD, $936D and their partners). Sets SID voice 2 control $D40B=$25 and attack/decay $D40C=$88, then adds the jump step counter $99 to A 25 times (ADC, carry not cleared), storing each sum in voice 2's frequency high byte $D408: the pitch follows the step count $99 (0-$14). Runs in the main loop, not in an interrupt.
Unused: 5 zero bytes before the delay fragment at $41D0.
Unreachable: a 256x256 delay loop (X and Y counting to wrap) that falls straight into score_add_1000. No reference to $41D0 anywhere in the image (searched by bytes).

Adds 1000 points to the score shown on the status line (six digits at columns 13-18 of character rows 23-24, drawn into the bitmap: the thousands digit is column 15, bitmap $3D38/$3E78). Digit glyphs are 16 bytes each at $1600 (top 8 bytes, then bottom 8; '0' at $1600 ... '9' at $1690). Copies the glyph whose address sits in the self-modified operands $41DD/$41E3 into column 15, counts the thousands in $40 and moves the operands on by $10. At the tenth step it redraws column 15 as '0', resets the operands to $10/$18, clears $40 and draws the next ten-thousands glyph (operands $4215/$421B) into column 14 ($3D30/$3E70), counted in $45; at ten of those, column 14 back to '0' and the next hundred-thousands glyph (operands $425B/$4261) into column 13 ($3D28/$3E68). Nothing carries past column 13: a tenth carry there would draw the 16 bytes at $16A0, which are not a digit. Called directly from 15 sites ($5C2F-$8AD5), one of them $8AD5 in $8AD0, through which the 10,000-75,000 adders $120E-$1247 call it; $1BA2-$1BBC resets the operands and $40/$45 at the start of a game.

Self-modified operand: low byte of the LDA $16x0,X that fetches the next thousands-digit glyph's top half ($10 after a reset at $1BA4, +$10 per 1000 points; $60 in the hand-over, a previous game's score).
Self-modified operand: low byte of the LDA $16x8,X that fetches the next thousands-digit glyph's bottom half (reset to $18 at $1BAF and $422A).
tenth thousand: carry into column 14

Self-modified operand: low byte of LDA $16x0,X for the next ten-thousands digit's top half (reset to $10 at $1BA7 and $426D, moved on at $4233-$4238: ADC #$0F with the carry that the CPX #$08 ending the copy loop at $4221 leaves set, so +$10).
Self-modified operand: low byte of LDA $16x8,X for the next ten-thousands digit's bottom half (reset to $18 at $1BB2 and $4272).
tenth ten-thousand: carry into column 13
Self-modified operand: low byte of LDA $16x0,X for the next hundred-thousands digit's top half (reset to $10 at $1BAA; moved on at $4279, never wrapped).
Self-modified operand: low byte of LDA $16x8,X for the next hundred-thousands digit's bottom half (reset to $18 at $1BB5; never wrapped).
86 bytes of unknown content (6 zeros, then values such as $FF, $CD, $32, $89, $BB). No absolute reference to $428A-$42DF was found in the image (searched by bytes); purpose not known.

Busy-wait: 80 passes of a 256-step X loop (about 0.1 s). Called after each of the three phases of a jump in rooms 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 11 and 4/7 (48 call sites, six per jump copy; room 8's jump uses its own copy, room8_jump_pause $6BC7), and once more from the disabled routine at $451F ($453F).
Unused: two NOPs ($EA) between delay_80x256 and room1_main_loop.

Room 1 (stage 1): one pass of the main loop, entered from $A81A (the room table's first entry, reached by JMP $A817 at $1BFC after room 1 is set up, and again at the end of every pass, $4601/$4609). If $F6=$30 (Mr Hat has just died) JSR $1FD7 puts him back (room1_respawn_position) and goes to game over if $D8=$40. Turns sprite 4 (Mr Hat) on. Joystick port 2, each test an exact value of $DC00: right ($77) one step right (INC $D008), walking frames $2C-$2E from $FD changing every 9 steps (counter $FB), voice 2 off ($1CF2), footstep tick ($1D04), 5x256 delay; down ($7D) shows the crouch frame $2A and stays while down is held, calling $6FDB (the timer and exit checks plus the floor handler) each pass; left ($7B) as right with frames $2F-$31 from $FF; fire ($6F) jumps (room1_jump). Stick up is not tested here: outside the lift it does nothing. Diagonals match none of the tests. Every pass then goes on to room1_rejump_check (JMP $444F at $43F2 when fire alone is not held), which tests fire with right ($67) or left ($6B), so those jump too, even from standing.

Room 1 jump, on fire alone ($DC00=$6F). Facing right (frame below $2F): frame $2D and 21 ($15) steps up and right, frame $2C and 21 steps right, frame $2E and 21 steps down and right; facing left: frames $30, $2F, $31 with the X steps reversed. Each step moves one pixel each way and calls $08A1 (the room 1 floor handler, so hazards and the lift work in the air); only the 21 rising steps play jump_step_sound with the step count $99 (voice 2 silenced once before them facing right, before each step facing left); delay_80x256 after each phase. So a jump is 63 pixels across and 21 high.

Copies the address in $C1/$C2 into the saved PC ($023A/$0239). Used by ; and G.
Prints eight bytes from ($C1) in hex, each after a space, advancing $C1/$C2; $988D prints the count already in $1D.
Prints $1D bytes from ($C1) in hex with spaces (entry of $988B with the count set by the caller).
Reads a hex byte; if one was typed stores it at ($C1) and reads it back, erroring ($9AED) if RAM did not take it; then advances $C1/$C2 and counts $1D down.
Points $C1/$C2 at the saved registers ($023B) and returns A = 5, their count.
Prints CR, '.' and the character in Y: the start of each line the monitor lists (':' memory, ';' registers, ',' disassembly, 'A' assembly).
Command R: prints the header 'PC SR AC XR YR SP' ($9FEA), then '.;' with the saved PC and the five saved registers.
Command M: reads a start and an end address and lists memory as '.:' lines of eight bytes until the end, the top of memory or STOP ($FFE1).
Command ; : reads a new PC (optional, into $0239/$023A) and five register values (SR, A, X, Y, SP) into $023B-$023F.
Command : : reads an address and up to eight hex bytes and stores them there ($98A1).
Command G: optionally takes an address as the new PC, restores SP, pushes PC and SR, loads A, X, Y from the saved registers and RTIs into the program.
Command X: restores SP and leaves through JMP ($A002), BASIC's warm start. With $01 = $36 (BASIC banked out, as the game runs) $A002 reads RAM, which is zero.
L and S arguments: device 1 by default, name length 0, name buffer $0240; reads "name" (up to 16 characters) and an optional ,device; returns with the last character read.
JMP ($0330): the KERNAL's LOAD vector, with A = 0 from the caller.
JMP ($0332): the KERNAL's SAVE vector.
Command L: reads the name and device ($9996) and loads through $99EF; a status bit 4 in $90 is an error.
Command S: reads name, device, start and end address ($AE/$AF gets the end) and saves through $99F2.
Prints the address $C2/$C1 as four hex digits.
Prints A as two hex digits (through $9A60 and $9A57).
Prints the character in X, then the one in A, with CHROUT ($FFD2).
Turns a value 0-15 in A into its hex digit character '0'-'9', 'A'-'F'.
Swaps the two address pointers $C1/$C2 and $C3/$C4.

Reads a four-digit hex address: the first byte into $C2 (high), the second into $C1 (low), each stored only if typed; carry clear if a field was empty. $9A7C, entered with the high byte already in A, stores it when carry is set and then reads the low byte.
Entry of $9A79 with the high byte already read into A (from $9ADF, after $9A8F): stores it in $C2 if carry is set, then reads a hex byte into $C1.
Reads two hex digits into A (via $2A); returns carry clear if two spaces were typed instead. $9A8F starts with the first character already in A.
Entry of $9A88 with the first character already read (from $9ADC and $9BF0).
Turns a hex digit character into its value 0-15.
Decrements the pointer $C3/$C4 (X = 2); a BIT $00A2 hides the LDX #$00 of the entry $9ABB.
Decrements the pointer $C1/$C2 (entered at the operand of the BIT at $9ABA, X = 0); sets $26 on wrap.
Reads characters until one is not a space.
Reads the command's first address into $C1/$C2 after the spaces, clearing $0100; any failure is the error ($9AED).
Reads one more address ($9A79); returns if one was given, else the error ($9AED).
Error: restores SP, prints $90 and '?' and returns to the prompt.
Prints X spaces.
Increments the pointer $C3/$C4.
Swaps $C1/$C2 with $28/$29 (the monitor's third address).
The assembler's branch offset: ($C3/$C4 - 2) - $C1/$C2 into $1E and Y.
Length from $C1/$C2 to $28/$29, into $1E and Y (through $9B33).
Length from $C1/$C2 to $C3/$C4, into $1E and Y; carry set while the end is not passed.
Command T: transfers (copies) memory from start-end to a destination, forwards or backwards so that overlapping ranges copy correctly.
Command F: fills start-end with a byte.
Command H: hunts start-end for up to 32 hex bytes or a 'text string (built in $0210), printing each address where it matches.
Command D: clears the screen and disassembles 22 lines from the address (kept in $20/$21 for the ',' command), then moves the cursor up.
The D page: clears the screen and disassembles 22 lines from $C1/$C2 (entered from ',' at $9DA2 to redraw).
Prints one disassembly line: '.,' address, the instruction's bytes ($9D1F), the mnemonic ($9D35) and the operand in its addressing mode (characters from $9F2A/$9F30); $9C72 skips the prefix.
Entry of $9C6A without the '.,' prefix (used by P at $9D74).
Prints A in hex keeping X (saved in $1C).
Returns in A/Y the address of the next instruction: $C1/$C2 plus the length in $1F plus one.
Adds the signed value in A (with carry) to $C1/$C2, returning A/Y: the branch target for the disassembler.
Classifies the opcode in A: looks up its addressing format in $9ED9 and $9F1D (into $2A, with the operand length in $1F) and returns the index of its mnemonic.
Prints the instruction's bytes from ($C1) padded to three columns.
Unpacks the three letters of mnemonic Y from $9F37 (left) and $9F77 (right), five bits each plus $3F, and prints them.
Prints a space; a BIT $0DA9 hides the LDA #$0D of $9D57.
Prints a carriage return (entered at the operand of the BIT at $9D56).
Command P: disassembles from the first address to the second without clearing the screen, stopping on STOP.
Command , : stores up to three bytes at the address (a line of the D page edited in place) and redraws the D page from $20/$21.

Prints the character in A unless it equals the byte in zero page $28 (CMP $28, not an immediate). Called only by the disassembler ($9CA6, $9CAE), after $9D35 has shifted the mnemonic out of $28 and left $00 or $80 there, so the addressing-mode characters it is given are always printed.

Command A: the one-line assembler. Packs the three mnemonic letters into $0210/$0211, reads the operand into $0210+, tries every opcode 0-255 against it ($9E03 loop) and, on a match, stores the instruction at ($C1), prints the next '.A' line with the next address and loops.
Re-entry of the assembler for the next line (from $9EB5).
Assembler: TAY, then $9EB9, so it matches the character in A twice against the next two typed operand characters. Used at $9E53 and $9E58 with A = '0' ($30).
Assembler: matches the character in A, then the one in Y, against the typed operand.
Assembler: matches one character (A, if not zero) against the typed operand.
Assembler: compares A with the typed operand character at $0210+$1D and advances $1D, keeping X.
Carry clear if A is '0'-'F' (from $30 to below $47), set otherwise.
The disassembler's addressing-format table, 68 bytes ($9ED9-$9F1C): two formats (nybbles) per byte, indexed by the opcode's bits in $9CD9.
14 bytes ($9F1D-$9F2A): for each format, which operand characters to print and the operand length (bits 0-1), read into $2A and $1F by $9CD9.
Base of the first addressing-mode character table (indexed 1-6 at $9CA3: , ) , # ( $); $9F2A itself is the last byte of $9F1D.
The first characters of the addressing modes, ',),#($' ($9F2B-$9F30).
Base of the second addressing-mode character table (indexed 1-6 at $9CA9); $9F30 itself is the last '$' of $9F2B.
The second characters of the addressing modes, 'Y', 0, 'X', '$', '$', 0 ($9F31-$9F36).
Packed mnemonics, left bytes, 64 entries ($9F37-$9F76): with $9F77 each pair holds three letters of five bits (plus $3F).
Packed mnemonics, right bytes, 64 entries ($9F77-$9FB6).
The 15 command letters searched by $9867: : ; R M G X L S T F H D P , A ($9FB7-$9FC5).

The handlers' addresses less one, 16 words ($9FC6-$9FE5), pushed and reached by RTS: : $9943, ; $9936, R $98CD, M $98F8, G $9957, X $998A, L $99F5, S $9A0D, T $9B3F, F $9B93, H $9BC1, D $9C39, P $9D5C, , $9D8B, A $9DAD. The 16th word ($9846) is never read: the search stops at 15 letters.
The high bytes of $9FC6 as $9871 reads them (LDA $9FC7,X).
Two addresses: $97FF, the BRK handler, which $97ED copies into $0316/$0317; and $97ED, the monitor's cold start.
High byte of the BRK handler's address, read by $97F3.
$97ED, the address of the monitor's cold start (nothing in the image reads it).
The R command's header: CR and '   PC  SR AC XR YR SP', 22 characters ($9FEA-$9FFF), printed by $98CD.

Restores Mr Hat's Y from $ABFF, reads $D01E to clear the collision latch, then $1D6D in the room whose $0400 is $6E, $1D86 elsewhere (both outside this range).

Is Mr Hat at a spot? A = flags, X = left, Y = right edge (exclusive) for $D008 (kept in $1E06/$1E07). $1020 stores A's low nybble in $1009 and returns a high nybble that should say whether to test the X high bit ($10); it reads $400B (always $FC) where it wrote $40BB, so it returns $F0 and the high-bit test at $A986 never runs. Of the 42 calls, 18 pass A = $01, which never asks for the check; 24 pass $10 or $11 ($AB47 passes $10 only after $4610 has moved him across the high bit; on its other path A still holds his X, whose low nybble becomes $1009). 23 of the 24 callers test the X high bit themselves first ($1200): 4 call only on the right half ($8E7C, $B192, $B350, $B37D) and behave the same either way, 19 only on the left half, where they match only because the check never runs. $AB47 is not gated. From $1E20: Mr Hat at X $C4-$F3 (no stick needed) and Y = $CC calls $55F5.

The shape is a bar across the top, a thin stem and a flared foot (it looks like a hanging lamp; not confirmed on screen).
